# Credential-access allow-list (E85_S02_T05), consumed by tests/credential-access-guard.bats.
#
# One entry per line:   <file>:<class>:<fixed-substring>  # <reason>
#   file             path relative to the repository root.
#   class            a scripts/scan-credential-patterns.sh class (gh-auth, aws-env, dotfile-path, home-ref,
#                    credential-file) for a MENTION, or `read` for an accepted READ of a credential value.
#   fixed-substring  literal text (no regex) that must occur in the matching line, so an entry excuses that line
#                    and not every future line of the file. It may contain colons.
#   reason           mandatory; the separator is the LAST two-spaces-hash-space on the line.
# Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.
#
# Every entry is derived from project/documentation/credential-access-audit.md: a mention is a row that audit
# classified "benign mention" (nothing is read), the single `read` entry is the row it marks "accepted by-design
# use" (user decision 2026-10-25). An entry that matches no line fails the guard (stale), so do not leave one
# behind when the line is removed. Do NOT add entries for skills/j-publish/scripts/validate_npm_env.sh or
# validate_ios_env.sh: E85_S02_T03 made them presence-only checks and the guard asserts they stay that way.

# --- accepted read (class `read`) -------------------------------------------------------------------------
skills/j-publish/scripts/ios_pipeline.sh:read:printenv "$var_name"  # accepted by-design use (audit, "Outside the five patterns"): resolve_env_value_from_ref looks up the env var named in publish.json's secrets block, so the value comes from the user's own environment; it is passed only to xcrun notarytool / altool or substituted into the scratch ExportOptions.plist, and the key file's contents are never read

# --- mentions: scripts/ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
scripts/pages-cutover.sh:gh-auth:if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then  # exit-code-only probe, output discarded, no token or account detail is captured
scripts/pages-cutover.sh:gh-auth:Run "gh auth login" with an account  # error text telling the user to log in themselves; the script runs nothing
scripts/resolve-tools.sh:dotfile-path:#   user     ${JENGA_USER_TOOLS_FILE:-$HOME/.jenga/tools.json}  # comment naming Jenga's own preferred-tools registry, not a credential file
scripts/resolve-tools.sh:home-ref:[ -n "${HOME:-}" ]  # tests whether HOME is set; reads no file and no secret
scripts/resolve-tools.sh:dotfile-path:USER_FILE="$HOME/.jenga/tools.json"  # path of Jenga's own preferred-tools registry, not a credential file
scripts/workflow/resolve-refs.sh:home-ref:such as ${HOME}, is not a reference  # header comment saying a non-reference token like ${HOME} is passed through unchanged; reads no file and no secret
